items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I’ve only played with him once and that was at this jazz party when it was still in Pennsylvania, about 1985.

ctx.x: Bass players, do they tend to try to work with you, like the gentlemen that you’re working with this weekend. Do you feel that the two of them are any different?

Well I haven’t played with Michael Moore yet. I will do that tonight. And I’ve only played with him once and that was at this jazz party when it was still in Pennsylvania, about 1985. That won’t be any problem. He’s a real light bass player.

items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

ctx.x: Which I think Joe tries to do here.

He has some groups. And Becky Kilgore and Dave have recorded together so they have material to work from. And then you have somebody like Dave McKenna, which is like a whole orchestra by himself. And so Joe knows how to do it and he knows how to mix guys — like Cal and I doing a duo together, and we have played together over the years. And he knows, to a degree, what’s going to work. And it’s just again, there’s not many groups around anymore, except a few very famous ones.
